definition: The support is a fixed unit square, D=sqrt(2). For even n>=8, p_i=(i/n, 0.5+(i%2)/n), i=0..n. All n-1 interior turns are pi/2. Each edge length/D is 1/n. The curve approaches y=0.5 with normalized Hausdorff distance <=1/(n*sqrt(2)).
limits: Formula-level counterexample for representing a smooth seam by a zigzag source-edge path on a fixed planar support; no C++ solver execution. The formula correctly measures the jagged curve. Hausdorff convergence alone does not imply curvature-energy convergence; this does not refute convergence for sufficiently smooth curve approximations.

assumptions: Two adjacent regions share a minimizing GMM component.
The only removed interface is a shared isolated closed contour, with no hard edges and soft confidence one.
Turning is disabled; no other boundary term changes.
